patch_description: The gradient ascent only optimizes a soft-min surrogate; the final score is the true hard min of triangle areas normalized by hull area. I add a deterministic hill-climb polishing stage that directly maximizes the true score, with **adaptive per-point step sizes** (per the recommendation): each point keeps its own step, halved when none of its trial moves improve, and occasionally regrown (×1.5, capped at 0.25) when a point has been skipped for many sweeps. This lets constrained points refine finely while hull points keep exploring, avoiding premature global step collapse. We polish only the top few gradient-optimized candidates to keep runtime bounded, then take the best true score across all candidates.
